description: Single-panel engineering stress–strain plot labelled (b); no caption was extracted, so all content below is read from the pixels. The abscissa is "ε_E, Engineering strain, %" spanning 0–80 (major ticks every 20) and the ordinate is "σ_E, Engineering stress, MPa" spanning 0–1500 (major ticks every 300). A legend headed "FexMn11Al1C(1050°C)" defines four solid curves coded by Mn content: 20Mn (black), 25Mn (red), 30Mn (green) and 34Mn (blue). The 20Mn curve reaches the highest stress level, plateauing just above the 900 MPa gridline and failing between the 20% and 40% strain gridlines — the lowest ductility. The 25Mn curve plateaus slightly below the 900 MPa gridline and extends to about the 50% strain gridline. The 30Mn curve yields well below the 900 gridline and hardens gradually, peaking near the 60% strain gridline. The 34Mn curve is softest at low strain and hardens monotonically to a maximum just below the 900 MPa gridline near 50–55% strain, then softens and drops just past the 60% gridline. All curves are smooth, with no serrated flow or yield-point elongation visible. The figure demonstrates that raising Mn from 20 to 34% lowers the flow stress at a given strain while markedly increasing elongation to fracture, with 30Mn and 34Mn converging to similar maximum stress.

subfigures.description: Engineering stress–strain curves (σ_E, MPa vs ε_E, %) for FexMn11Al1C(1050°C) with four Mn levels: 20Mn (black), 25Mn (red), 30Mn (green), 34Mn (blue). Higher Mn shifts curves downward in stress but extends strain to fracture; black fails earliest (~20–40% gridlines), red near 50%, green and blue just past 60%.

observations.observation: The image is a single engineering stress–strain plot labelled (b), with x-axis 'ε_E, Engineering strain, %' from 0 to 80 (ticks every 20) and y-axis 'σ_E, Engineering stress, MPa' from 0 to 1500 (ticks every 300).
The legend header reads 'FexMn11Al1C(1050°C)' and lists four colour-coded conditions: 20Mn (black), 25Mn (red), 30Mn (green) and 34Mn (blue).

The 20Mn (black) curve reaches the highest stress of the four, plateauing just above the 900 MPa gridline and below the 1200 MPa gridline, and terminates between the 20% and 40% strain gridlines, giving the lowest elongation.
The 25Mn (red) curve plateaus slightly below the 900 MPa gridline and extends to approximately the 50% strain gridline before a sharp stress drop.
The 30Mn (green) curve yields between the 600 and 900 MPa gridlines and hardens gradually to its maximum near the 60% strain gridline, where it drops steeply.

The 34Mn (blue) curve is the lowest of the four at small strains (between the 300 and 600 MPa gridlines) and rises monotonically to a maximum just below the 900 MPa gridline at roughly 50–55% strain, then softens and drops just past the 60% strain gridline.
Increasing Mn content from 20 to 34% lowers the flow stress at a given strain but increases the strain to fracture, i.e. strength and ductility trade off with Mn level.
The 30Mn and 34Mn curves converge to comparable maximum stress near the end of their deformation, despite very different yield stresses.
All four curves are smooth; no serrated flow, Lüders plateau or distinct yield-point elongation is visible.
No numeric data labels, UTS values or elongation values are printed on the curves; only gridline positions are available.
